Find the general-purpose numeric clamp(value, min, max) helper that the main math package exports for general use — not any package-local copy meant only for that package's own internal use — and list at least 6 distinct files elsewhere in the codebase that call it.

Find the public-API wrapper specifically and list every file that calls it, other than where it's defined.

In this repository, first find every file that calls the standalone mutateElement function exported by the element package — the helper that applies an in-place update to a single element and bumps its version — as opposed to the same-named method on the Scene class. Then, considering only those files, report which of them also call the standalone getNonDeletedElements helper exported by that same package, as opposed to the same-named Scene method or a module-local helper of the same name. A file that only re-exports one of these symbols without calling it does not count. Your final answer must list only the files that satisfy both conditions, each as a full repo-relative path.

oracle.rubric: The question: which files in the Excalidraw repo call BOTH the standalone mutateElement function exported by the element package AND the standalone getNonDeletedElements function exported by that same package. Ground truth: exactly two files — packages/element/src/frame.ts and packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFrame.ts. PASS only if the answer's final list of files is exactly those two. FAIL if either is missing from the final list, or if the final list contains any other file. Files that the answer explicitly rules out or presents as excluded do not count as part of its final list. Wrong entries that must FAIL if presented as part of the answer: packages/excalidraw/clipboard.ts, packages/element/src/Scene.ts, packages/element/src/binding.ts, packages/element/src/linearElementEditor.ts and packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx (these call mutateElement, but reach getNonDeletedElements only as the Scene class method or a module-local helper of the same name, or not at all); packages/excalidraw/index.tsx (it re-exports both symbols and calls neither); and files such as packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx, actionFlip.ts, actionDeleteSelected.tsx or anything under packages/excalidraw/components/Stats/ (these call getNonDeletedElements but not the standalone mutateElement). Formatting, ordering, prose and extra correct commentary do not matter.

prompt: In this repository, first find every class that implements the Trail interface, including classes that only get it indirectly by extending another Trail implementation. Then, of those classes, report which ones are defined in a file that also calls pointFrom (the helper that constructs a 2D point value) and which ones are not. Name the classes on both sides of that split.

oracle.rubric: The answer is about classes implementing the Trail interface in the Excalidraw repo, split by whether the class's own file calls pointFrom. Ground truth: exactly five classes implement Trail — AnimatedTrail, LaserTrails, DrawShapeTrail (all three declare `implements Trail`), plus EraserTrail and LassoTrail (which implement it indirectly by extending AnimatedTrail). Of these, the files defining DrawShapeTrail, EraserTrail and LassoTrail call pointFrom; the files defining AnimatedTrail and LaserTrails do not. PASS only if the answer names DrawShapeTrail, EraserTrail and LassoTrail as the ones whose files call pointFrom AND states that AnimatedTrail and LaserTrails do not. FAIL if it omits any of DrawShapeTrail/EraserTrail/LassoTrail from the calling side, if it claims AnimatedTrail or LaserTrails calls pointFrom, or if it presents some class other than these five as a Trail implementation. Wording, ordering, and extra correct detail such as file paths or line numbers do not matter.

prompt: In this repository, start from mutateElement — the helper that applies an in-place update to a single element and bumps its version. When the update changes an element's points, it delegates to a small helper imported from another workspace package to derive the element's width and height from that points array. Name that helper, then list every other file in the repository that calls the same helper, excluding the file that defines it and excluding mutateElement's own file. Give full repo-relative paths.

In this repository, I'm about to change the signature of the getElementAbsoluteCoords function (the helper that computes an element's absolute bounding coordinates, accounting for rotation) — for example, adding a new required parameter. Before making the change, list at least 10 distinct files elsewhere in the codebase that call it and would need their call sites updated. Give each file's full repo-relative path.

In this repository, there is an exported helper function named getRectangleBoxAbsoluteCoords. Before removing it as apparent dead code, check thoroughly: does anything anywhere in the repository — production code, tests, or any other package — actually call it? State your conclusion (safe to delete, or not) and, if it is called anywhere, name every file that calls it.

oracle.rubric: The question is whether getRectangleBoxAbsoluteCoords (exported from packages/element/src/bounds.ts) has any real caller anywhere in the Excalidraw repository, including tests. Ground truth, independently verified with the TypeScript language service (project-wide reference search, tests included): it has ZERO references anywhere outside its own declaration — it is genuinely unused, dead code, and safe to delete. PASS only if the answer's final conclusion states it is unused/has no callers and that it is safe to delete (or clearly equivalent wording), and does not claim any real caller/file for it. FAIL if the answer claims any file (other than its own defining file, if mentioned only as the declaration site) calls it, if it concludes it is NOT safe to delete, or if it hedges to an unclear/uncertain conclusion instead of stating it is unused and safe to delete. Wording, ordering, and extra correct commentary do not matter.

prompt: Users report that adding the same shape library twice — clicking "Add to Excalidraw" on a library they already have, or opening the same .excalidrawlib file again — ends up with every item in it duplicated in their library, instead of the editor recognising that those items are already there. The same thing happens to items that reached the user by some other route (another document, another session, a library someone else re-exported): they are indistinguishable on canvas from shapes already in the library, and they still get added again. There is de-duplication logic already, and it catches none of this. Find the root cause and fix it in the actual code, so that an item indistinguishable from one already in the library is recognised as a duplicate no matter where it came from, while genuinely different items are still added and items that differ only in how many shapes they contain, or in what order those shapes are stacked, are still treated as different.

Moving an elbow arrow so that it lands exactly on x = 0 (or exactly on y = 0) silently leaves it at its old position instead — the identical move to any non-zero coordinate works fine, nothing throws, and no error is logged. Find the root cause and fix it in the actual code, without changing how elbow arrows behave for any non-zero destination.

A user with a labelled arrow — an arrow that has bound text on it — reports that entering line-editing mode on it (the "Edit arrow" / "Edit line" action) sometimes crashes the editor with an internal assertion instead of opening the editor. The same action on the same kind of arrow works fine in other documents, so it depends on the document rather than on the arrow. Find the root cause and fix it in the actual code, without changing when the action is offered or how line editing behaves for the arrows it already works on.

In this repository, there's a component used throughout the dropdown-menu UI that consumers import as DropdownMenuGroup. Find where it's actually declared — including what it's really named inside its own source file, since the value it wraps is default-exported under a different local name than the one it's imported under — and report the file it lives in plus that real internal name.

In this repository's laser-pointer package, find the plerp function (a point-interpolation helper) and determine whether any file calls it through a namespace-style import (e.g. `import * as x from "..."` followed by `x.plerp(...)`) rather than a plain named import of plerp itself. If such a call exists, name the calling file.

In this repository, find the setLanguage function in the i18n module. It dynamically imports a locale data file using a computed path. Can the exact locale file it will load be determined statically just by reading the code, or does it depend on a runtime value? Explain which, and if it depends on a runtime value, say what that value is.

oracle.rubric: The question is about setLanguage in packages/excalidraw/i18n.ts, which does `await import(`./locales/${currentLang.code}.json`)` after assigning `currentLang = lang` from its own `lang` parameter. Ground truth: the exact locale file cannot be determined statically just by reading the code - it depends on the runtime value of the `lang` argument passed to setLanguage (equivalently, `currentLang.code` / the language code in effect when it's called), not on any compile-time constant. PASS if the answer correctly states that the exact target file cannot be statically determined and depends on a runtime value (e.g., the language code argument, `currentLang.code`, or an equivalent description of a runtime-supplied language selection), and does not claim a single fixed locale file (e.g. en.json) as the only possible target. FAIL if the answer claims the import always resolves to one specific fixed locale file, or omits that the target depends on a runtime-determined language code.
